reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that TiC forms from carbon impurities and contributes to strengthening in CoCrFeNiTix alloys, but it does not support the premise that the baseline equimolar alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution without precipitates, nor does it provide data on the specific carbon level needed for fine dispersion. The hypothesis overstates the evidence by assuming the baseline state is precipitate-free and that a specific carbon addition will yield the desired microstructure.
premises: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can exist as a single-phase FCC solid solution with minimal carbon impurities
Low hardness and strength in this alloy are due to the absence of secondary-phase precipitates
TiC precipitates form in CoCrFeNiTi when carbon is present during sintering
TiC precipitates act as strong barriers to dislocation motion, increasing strength and hardness
A carbon addition of ~0.05 wt% will produce fine, uniformly dispersed TiC precipitates
